messages:
maria: noticed something odd in backup audits this morning - a handful of recent snapshots uploaded to s3://redwood-prod-archives show no SSE headers in the upload logs. unsure if uploader used SSE-C or the metadata was stripped. pinging ops.
sam: damn, do you have keys/ids for the objects? can you paste a sample log line?
maria: here - from the backup-agent logs (sanitized):
```
2026-03-20T07:12:03Z uploader INFO upload complete key=backups/2026-03-19/tenant-42/snap-abc123.tar.gz size=2.1G headers={} http_status=200
```
no x-amz-server-side-encryption in headers. object metadata in S3 console also missing SSE headers.
alex: are these all the same service account/uploader? maybe an IAM change rolled out overnight.
tess: checking IAM change logs...found a role policy update at 2026-03-20T06:55:00Z: `backup-uploader` had new inline policy that removed `kms:Encrypt` on the CMK used for sse-kms (KMS Key: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/abcd-ef12). that would cause agent to fallback to client-side no-encryption if misconfigured.
maria: @tess can you link the policy diff? we need to know if this was intentional.
tess: pasted diff snippet: `- "kms:Encrypt": ["arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/abcd-ef12"]` and an admin comment "scope cleanup". looks like accidental removal.
oncall-sre: immediate ask: can we block new snapshot uploads to that bucket until we confirm? we should also revoke the uploader role for prod while investigating.
sam: I can run an S3 bucket policy quick-block and create a deny for PutObject from that principal. will that break restores? only new uploads blocked, reads unaffected.
alex: +1 for deny on PutObject from `arn:aws:iam::123456:role/backup-uploader`. also add MFA/condition until we sort the RBAC change.
opsbot: runbook step 1 executed: applied temporary PutObject deny for principal backup-uploader on s3://redwood-prod-archives at 2026-03-20T07:22:45Z. created ticket INF-5342.
security-bot: audit query: found 7 objects uploaded between 2026-03-20T06:58 and 2026-03-20T07:15 without SSE headers. objects list: [snap-abc123.tar.gz, snap-def456.tar.gz, snap-ghi789.tar.gz, snap-jkl012.tar.gz, snap-mno345.tar.gz, snap-pqr678.tar.gz, snap-stu901.tar.gz].
maria: can we identify if those are restorable/decrypted? if software wrote unencrypted blobs, they are cleartext at rest.
sam: they are stored cleartext since S3 shows no SSE metadata. immediate concern: tenant data exposure. we need to escalate to compliance and notify SLA list if PII involved.
alex: action items: 1) revoke backup-uploader IAM role or attach explicit kms:Encrypt allow for CMK 2) re-ingest a re-encrypted copy of affected objects from our secure vault (if original plaintext still available) 3) run a restore test to verify integrity 4) add guardrails to prevent future IAM rollbacks.
tess: on the IAM front: I recommend restoring previous inline policy from git history (we have the old policy in infra repo). then create a least-privileged grant that only allows kms:Encrypt on that specific CMK for uploader and only from specific source IPs. also create an enforcement check in PR CI.
oncall-sre: who can rotate the CMK if we suspect key compromise? rotating CMK will not re-encrypt existing objects automatically; we'd need to re-upload.
sam: wkf: first restore-policy: restore previous policy, reapply, then run a small re-upload pipeline for those objects. created a short script to re-encrypt and re-upload via aws cli using kms:Encrypt: 
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-prod-archives/backups/2026-03-19/tenant-42/snap-abc123.tar.gz - | 
aws s3 cp - s3://redwood-prod-archives/backups/2026-03-19/tenant-42/snap-abc123.tar.gz --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/abcd-ef12
```
(note: pipeline uses streaming to avoid local disk)
maria: compliance asks for an audit timeline + list of affected tenants. I started a spreadsheet. @sam can you run a CloudTrail query for PutObject events by that role between those times and export principals/tenants.
sam: running CloudTrail: `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=PutObject --start-time 2026-03-20T06:50:00Z --end-time 2026-03-20T07:30:00Z` filtering on principal. results show 7 PutObject events by role, tenant IDs included in object key path.
security-bot: flagged incident SEV-3 and notified compliance channel with initial context. recommended communication template: short notice to affected tenants that a subset of backups were uploaded without SSE; we are re-encrypting and will validate integrity; no evidence of exfiltration as of now.
alex: long-term fixes: - add an IAM guard in policy-catalog that disallows PRs removing kms:Encrypt from uploader roles for keys tagged `backup:encrypted=true` - add CloudWatch metric alarm for PutObject events missing SSE header - add pre-apply terraform test that simulates the IAM diff
maria: +1 on the alarm. also we should add an S3 bucket-level default encryption policy (SSE-KMS) to make misconfigurations less likely.
tess: I've opened PR in infra to: 1) revert the inline change 2) add bucket default encryption 3) add CI gate. PR: https://git.internal/infra/terraform/pulls/482
oncall-sre: next ops steps: sam to finish re-encrypt pipeline for 7 objects and verify checksums. maria to prepare tenant notification draft. alex/tess to harden IAM + infra. I will keep bucket deny in place until we confirm pipeline success.
sam: starting re-encrypt job now, ETA ~20m. will post checksum diffs when done.
maria: thanks all. please add any audit links to INF-5342 ticket.
